issue_context.title: test_path_is_network_fs_harder fails in build environments
issue_context.body:
```
/* test_path_is_network_fs_harder */
src/test/test-mount-util.c:541: Assertion failed: expected "path_is_network_fs_harder("/dev")" to succeed but got the following error: Invalid argument
```

the test makes assumption about the running environment, but they are out of its control. There are no guarantees about any of the external directories or mount points or anything else in a build environment. This needs to be dropped or changed to work everywhere, under any condition.

https://buildd.debian.org/status/fetch.php?pkg=systemd&arch=amd64&ver=257%7Erc1-2&stamp=1730977643&raw=0

Regression introduced by https://github.com/systemd/systemd/commit/d49d95df0a260aaca9a3fdd1e6ce535592a53bca

review_comments: check for permission errors and skip instead
In this case, we know the path is a temporary directory, and we have a capability to do that.

Not necessarily, mounting could be blocked, for example via seccomp, or selinux, or many other ways. This is a unit test, it cannot assert on permissions, it needs to detect and gracefully skip on denials.

Theoretically true, but if that happens, many test cases in this test will fail, not only here.
Let's address such theoretical concern all places if we really want to run the unit test on such spurious or too strict system.
